behavior: 2-line lead-in comment (5421-5422): `_layerSel` is a multi-selection of layer rows (Cmd/Ctrl+click toggles, Shift+click ranges); operations like Delete apply to the whole set.
Declaration (5423): `var _layerSel=[];` — module-level (function-scope-free, script top-level `var`), starts empty.

8-line comment (5424-5431) documents the 2026-07-31 unification pass that added `_layerSelAnchor`: both row handlers (Animation 2D's own, and Motion's `renderLayerListMotion`) previously derived the Shift-range anchor from `_layerSel[0]` — the CURRENT first element of the live array — which silently relocates after any Shift-click toward a LOWER index (the rebuilt range's `[0]` is `min(anchor,idx)`, not the original anchor); layer-inout.js's own `_barAnchorLi` already avoided this exact drift with a dedicated variable Shift never touches, and this declaration is the same contract for the layer list: set on every plain click and Ctrl-toggle, read-only for Shift.

packets.responsibility: Pure reader shared by `renderLayerList()` and `renderTimeline()` (and, transitively, `computeLayerRenderOrder` below) that resolves every real Folder-layer (`ld.isFolderLayer`) to the set of OTHER layer indices whose `parentLayerUid` points at it, so both renderers agree on which rows nest under which folder — independent of physical array adjacency.
behavior: 20-line lead-in comment (5543-5564): shared by `renderLayerList()`/`renderTimeline()` so the layer list and the frame grid always agree on visible rows; a folder header entry appears once, right before the first of its consecutive member layers, a collapsed folder's members are marked `hidden:true` rather than omitted so callers needing the real layer index (frame-grid columns) can still find it. Folder LAYER (2026-08, `ld.isFolderLayer` — distinct from the plain `ld.folderId`/`state.layerFolders` UI-only grouping declared later in this scope) is a real `state.layers[]` entry whose children are every OTHER layer with `parentLayerUid===` this folder's own uid, wherever they physically sit in the array (SMMotion's existing parenting mechanism doesn't require adjacency); resolved once up front so the main high-to-low loop in `computeLayerRenderOrder` can splice a folder's children in as nested entries right after it. A layer that is ITSELF a folder is never absorbed as someone else's child — nested folders are v1-unsupported (mirrors engine.rs's `is_folder_layer` doc comment, out of scope); the UI drop handler `moveLayerReorder` (out of scope) additionally refuses to let a drag create this situation.
Function declaration (5565): `function folderLayerChildMap(){`.
State init (5566): `var folderUidByIdx={},childrenOf={},childOf={};`.

Pass 1, folder discovery (5567-5573, high-to-low `for(var k=state.layers.length-1;k>=0;k--)`): for each `lk` with `lk.isFolderLayer`, resolves its uid via `(window.SMMotion&&SMMotion.ensureLayerUid)?SMMotion.ensureLayerUid(lk):lk.layerUid` (out of scope, motion.js:3519) and records `folderUidByIdx[k]=fuid` if truthy.

Pass 2, child resolution (5574-5585, high-to-low `for(var k2=...)`): skips any `lk2` with no `parentLayerUid` or that is itself a folder (5576); for each remaining layer, scans `folderUidByIdx` for a matching `parentLayerUid` (5577-5584) and, on the first match, records `childrenOf[fidx].push(k2)` and `childOf[k2]=fidx`, then `break`s — a layer can be the child of at most one folder in this map (first match by folder-index-iteration-order wins, not by any declared priority).
Return (5586): `return {childrenOf:childrenOf,childOf:childOf};` — a fresh object literal on every call, no caching.
